name: Today's Report
headline: First-time buyers are 40 for a second straight year, NAR says; the 30-year is 7.18%.
teaser: The typical first-time buyer is 40 for a second straight year, New York passed the Bay Area in tech workers, the 30-year is 7.18%, and Brent fell 5.85%.

sections.label: Real estate
sections.html:
Rates barely moved. Mortgage News Daily's 30-year average edged up 0.01 to 7.18% Monday, and the 15-year held at 6.83%. The 30-year is 0.09 lower than a week ago and 0.30 lower than a month ago. At 7.18%, a Fremont buyer at today's $1,298,500 median with 20% down would pay about $7,037 a month in principal and interest, $212 less than a month ago.

First-time buyers are 40, again. The typical first-time buyer is 40 years old for the second year in a row, the record high, according to the National Association of REALTORS 2026 Profile of Home Buyers and Sellers. In 1991 the median first-time buyer was 28, and since 2010 the age has climbed from 30. First-time buyers made up 22% of purchases, up slightly from last year's record low of 21%.

Cash and patience. A record 10% of first-time buyers paid all cash; those buyers had a median age of 54, against 38 for first-time buyers who financed. Sellers had owned their homes a median of 12 years, also a record.

What it means for you. If you rent and are saving for a first home, you are not behind. The typical first-time buyer is now 40, and those who finance are a little younger, at 38. Every quarter point on the median Fremont home is about $177 a month. Sellers, 187 homes in our five cities have been listed 60 days or longer, from 175 yesterday.

Today's count. Board wide: 2,419 listings across the 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, down from 2,451, with 147 coming soon and 148 brand new. The five city ledger carries 623 live listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City, 555 on the market and 68 coming soon, down from 624.

Fremont holds 214 live listings: 166 active, 32 coming soon and 15 brand new, with a median on market list price of $1,298,500 at $790 a square foot and a typical listing out 35 days. Hayward carries 176, Milpitas 94, Newark 78 and Union City 61. Across all five cities the median is $1,024,950 at $665 a square foot, 275 homes are priced under a million, and 187 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

images.alt: Line chart of the median age of first-time U.S. home buyers from 1981 to 2026. It was 29 in 1981, a low of 28 in 1991, 30 in 2010, 33 in 2020, 36 in 2022, 38 in 2024, and 40 in both 2025 and 2026, the record high.
images.caption: The median first-time buyer is 40 for the second straight year, a record; in 1991 it was 28.

sections.label: Economy
sections.html:
New York passed the Bay Area in tech workers. Between 2022 and 2025 the New York metro added 30,640 tech workers to reach 394,300, while the San Francisco Bay Area lost 23,900 to 375,730, CBRE's Scoring Tech Talent 2026 report found. CBRE says that is partly due to layoffs of tech workers outside artificial intelligence in the Bay Area. The Bay Area still ranks first in CBRE's overall tech talent scorecard.

Tech jobs are not only at tech companies. CBRE counts tech jobs in every industry, and Market Briefs notes that nearly two thirds of New York's tech workers work outside tech companies, at employers like banks and media firms.

Bonds, metals and oil. Treasury has the 10-Year at 4.88% Monday, up 0.02; Market Briefs printed 4.87%. Gold settled at $4,114.50, up 0.97% (Market Briefs had $4,122 and 0.19%, a late evening price). Silver settled at $52.69, up 1.45%, and Brent at $92.57, down 5.85%. This morning at 7:50 AM PT gold is lower near $4,057 and Brent near $90.51.

images.alt: Slope chart of tech talent jobs by metro in 2022 and 2025. The San Francisco Bay Area fell from 399,600 to 375,700, down 6.0%. The New York metro rose from 363,700 to 394,300, up 8.4%, passing the Bay Area.
images.caption: New York added 30,640 tech workers from 2022 to 2025 while the Bay Area lost 23,900.

sections.label: Stocks
sections.html: Stocks rebounded Monday. The Nasdaq closed up 2.74%, the S&P 500 2.35% and the Dow 2.15%, or about 1,104 points. Nvidia was the exception, down 4.27%, Market Briefs reported. Tuesday is giving some of it back: at 7:50 AM PT the S&P 500 is down 0.76%, the Nasdaq 0.93% and the Dow 0.69%.

sections.label: Crypto
sections.html: Crypto is still sliding. Over 24 hours Bitcoin is down 2.89% near $73,232, Ether 5.73% near $2,021.98 and XRP 6.44% near $1.04, live from CoinGecko at 7:50 AM PT. Market Briefs reported that Bitcoin touched $73,761 on Sunday, its lowest since August, before bouncing above $75,000; this morning it is below that Sunday low.
